problems: The labels collide: the 'right lip of the rim' label runs into the 'right shoulder of the belly' and 'foot of the D-handle' labels, and the labels are cut off at the frame edge ('tip of the spilled salt stre'). Several labels are unreadable.
The D-handle is not legible. Its foot star (43409) sits almost on top of the right-shoulder star (43825), so there is no visible handle arc between the right lip (44824) and the foot.
The figure is small and cramped in the lower-middle of the frame, with the rim, belly and spill packed into roughly 200x100 px. The rest of the canvas is empty star field.
There is no visible neck linking the left rim (45902) to the belly. The rim is a flat gold line, so the pot reads more as a bowl or sack than as a salt pot.

The blue closed loop is a plausible silhouette and is not a copy of the gold lines, and the figure is upright (rim on top, spill falling to the lower right). The gold lines themselves are straight and sit over the silhouette, which weakens the figure.
output.advice: Enlarge the whole figure about 2x and center it in the frame. Spread the right-shoulder star 43825 and the handle-foot star 43409 apart so they are clearly separate, and draw a curved D-handle arc from the right lip 44824 out to 43409. Add a short neck between the left rim 45902 and the belly. Keep the belly silhouette rounded at its widest point near 46026. Offset labels with leader lines so they do not overlap, and stop the spill label from running off the right edge. Make the blue silhouette the dominant shape and reduce the weight of the gold lines so they do not hide it. Result: a salt pot with a D-handle and a spill, with the labels legible.
